verdict.root_cause: Frontend is the reporter, not the fault. It started once and stayed up, has no recorded change, and all its errors come from outbound grpc-js client calls [tr_8ecdbe507b97, tr_2798b6260429]. The innermost detail names one peer: a checkout-path cart lookup failing with TCP connect refused to a resolved IP on port 7070, the cart service port [tr_8ecdbe507b97]. Connection refused with a resolved address means no listener was accepting — not slowness, DNS, TLS or authz, all excluded on the shape of the statuses. checkoutservice merely relays it: its error ratio did not escalate in-window and was worse in the preceding baseline [tr_e88820eb7ba4], with no change record [tr_e95b2ea2ec30]. currencyservice served normally throughout [tr_eb5d44e30a73]. Frontend's bursty ~12% mean / ~30% peak with clean intervals [tr_51946a056a73] fits a peer intermittently absent. What made cart stop listening was never measured: no cartservice dispatch was run and the trace backend returned 503 [tr_b25a7c830a93], so I name the failing service but not the mechanism inside it.
verdict.reasoning: Attribution rests on one positive artifact rather than on silence: the propagated dial error identifies a concrete peer and port (7070) refusing connections during a checkout cart fetch [tr_8ecdbe507b97], and that same result rules out timeout, DNS, TLS and frontend-local causes. Frontend and checkoutservice both have empty change logs and checkoutservice's errors moved down, not up [tr_e88820eb7ba4] — the pattern of a middle tier passing through a downstream refusal. The intermittency in frontend's error ratio [tr_51946a056a73] argues cart was cycling rather than hard down. I withhold a mechanism class because cartservice itself was never observed: no restart counts, resource series, or change history, and no spans [tr_b25a7c830a93].
open_questions: cartservice was never queried directly — restarts, OOM kills, image/config changes and listener state on 7070 are all unobserved.
No trace or latency data exists (backend 503), so the deepest erroring span and any lead/lag between cart, checkout and frontend is unestablished.
checkoutservice's high pre-incident baseline error ratio suggests degradation predating the declared window; onset time is unsettled.

alternatives.root_cause: cartservice pods are being killed for exceeding a memory limit, so the listener disappears intermittently and connections are refused.
alternatives.why_not: Fits the intermittent refused-connection pattern, but no cartservice memory, restart or kill evidence was ever gathered; this is a mechanism story with no supporting dispatch.

alternatives.root_cause: A cartservice deploy shipped an artifact that cannot stay up, leaving port 7070 unbound between restart attempts.
alternatives.why_not: Change history was only queried at seed radius for frontend and checkoutservice [tr_2798b6260429, tr_e95b2ea2ec30], so no cart change is either confirmed or excluded.

proposal.expected_effect: Recreating cartservice should restore a listener on 7070. Frontend's Loki stream should stop emitting `14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established` and the wrapped `13 INTERNAL` cart-lookup detail with connect-refused to :7070 within ~2 minutes, and frontend's error-ratio series should fall from its ~11.7% mean / ~30% peak bursty shape to a near-zero floor across four consecutive 2m samples. Confirmation must come from logs and metrics only: the trace backend is returning 503.
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if connect-refused-to-7070 lines persist after cartservice is back up (fault is not the listener), or if they stop and return inside the window (cartservice is crash-looping or OOM-killed and the restart only resets the clock), or if the container will not start at all (points at an unqueried cartservice image/config change).
proposal.risk: The mechanism inside cartservice was never measured — no restart count, exit code, OOM record or change history for it. If the cause is an OOM loop or a bad image, the restart re-enters the same failure and destroys the exit state that would identify it; restart_service is irreversible. It also discards in-process cart state, so in-flight checkouts may lose carts — a new failure that hides behind a healthy-looking error ratio.
proposal.blast_radius: cartservice alone for the duration of the recreate. Its inbound callers in this graph are frontend (direct) and checkoutservice (via the cart lookup on the checkout path); both see connection resets during the recreate, which will briefly raise the same error ratio we expect to fall. Users mid-checkout are the human-visible edge.

triage_judgement.reasoning: Critical alerts on frontend and checkoutservice within seconds of each other, plus loadgenerator, indicate a real user-facing failure with no open incident to attribute it to. Shared downstream dependencies make a common cause plausible but the alerts alone don't point to one.
